games.reason: Both chains have only in-vitro binding predictions and lack matched-context ChIP-seq support, so neither establishes occupancy or downstream effects. A is somewhat better supported because ZNF696 has a single-member family model, predicts a clear alt-G binding advantage, and is detected in HCT 116 (E14); the AP-2 model also predicts an allele preference, but TFAP2A and TFAP2C are expressed alongside TFAP2E, leaving greater ambiguity about which member acts (E15). This is a modest distinction, not evidence of a functional regulatory or colorectal-cancer effect.

Both chains have an expressed TF and an in-vitro model predicting their stated allele direction, while neither has matched-context ChIP-seq support (E12). The predictions are therefore not evidence of occupancy in HCT 116. The ZNF696 prediction has the larger allelic contrast (z 23.6; site strength 21.9 to 95.1) than the TFAP2E prediction (z -18.37; site strength 97.4 to 70.8), and TFAP2A and TFAP2C are also expressed, leaving more ambiguity about which AP-2 member could act (E14, E15). This modestly favors B; it does not establish the element, target gene, or colorectal-cancer link.
